root.name: Philidor Defense: Boden Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 exd4 4. Qxd4 Bd7

overview: White recaptures 4.Qxd4 and Black plays the quiet ...Bd7, avoiding ...Nc6 with tempo. White usually continues Bc4 and Nc3 with a space edge and Black develops with ...Nf6 and ...Nc6. The game is passive for Black and quiet for White.

white_ideas.idea: Play Bc4, Nc3 and a quick castle, using the central queen
Use extra space and the lead in development

typical_structures.structure: White e4 pawn against Black d6 pawn
Open d-file with queens still on

character.notes: Passive for Black but with few tactics.

soundness.notes: Black is a little passive but playable.

structure.notes: After exd4 the d-file is half open for both.

approach.notes: A sideline of an uncommon defence.

character.reason: Black is cramped but hard to break down and White has no forcing line.

soundness.reason: Black is a bit passive but fine.

structure.reason: The d-pawns trade, leaving a half-open d-file and an e4/d6 asymmetry.

approach.reason: Less common than the Philidor main line but respectable.

level.reason: Clear plans but passive and little to learn.

plans.reason: White keeps more space with the queen on d4.
